lesson.grammar_point: future forms: will, be going to and present continuous

extra_audio.text: Thank you for your time. Let me outline where Dataside is today, and where it is going. Dataside is a data and AI company with almost three hundred people in Brazil. We have grown every year since 2015, and banking has become our biggest growth driver. Next year, we are going to expand into Mexico, and we are opening an office in Austin in March. With the right partner, this business will double in five years, and I will stay as CEO for three years. That is the plan. I am happy to take your questions now.

I listen to about two hundred pitches a year, and I can tell you when I stop listening. It is when the founder spends four minutes on the history of the company. I already read the history. What I want to hear is where you are going. What are you going to do with the money? What is already signed? What do you think will happen to your market? Give me the future in a clear structure, and I will give you my attention.

The first time I pitched my company to an American fund, I talked about our past for almost the whole meeting. They were polite, and they never called back. The second time, I changed the order. One minute on who we are, one minute on what we have done, and then the future: we are opening an office in Chicago in June, we are going to double the sales team, and this market will grow thirty percent a year. They asked me questions for forty minutes.
